text: There are all kinds of books about the\nCrown Tundra!
Which book would you like to read?
Would you like to check any of the other books?

The king was a great Pokémon that brought
abundance to our cold land.\c
With a sweep of its right hand, the land would be
blanketed in verdant grasses and blooms.\c
With a sweep of its left hand, the fruit of the
fields would ripen and grow heavy.\c
Its great crown of green gleaming, the king
galloped across the land astride its proud steed.\c
And in their footsteps, buds would burst from the
soil, and rich life was born across the region.\c
And so we worshiped the Pokémon and paid it
all due tribute as king.

The horse Pokémon gave over its power to serve
the king and carry it hither and thither.\c
The two even became one for a time, combining
their strength to create a forest in a single night.\c
This proud steed had been a wild thing once,
ravaging the village crops and causing much woe.\c
But the king, in all its greatness, brought this
fierce creature to heel and secured its loyalty.\c
And for each among us who claims the steed’s
hide was black as the midnight gloom in which
[VAR FF00(0006)]ghosts[VAR FF00(0000)] appear, there is another who claims it was
white as a block of solid [VAR FF00(0006)]ice[VAR FF00(0000)].\c
None alive can now say which is the truth.

Through these reins did the king send its power,
in order to tame and control its proud steed.\c
The reins, in fact, were made by the hands of
the people, in thanks for the plenty brought by
the king.\c
These reins bound not only the horse and the
king to one another—they bound the people to
the king as well.\c
At the dawning of each new year, we must never
forget to gift the king with this offering.\c
Let the radiant flower and the mane of the steed
be woven together to bind us all in faith.\c
Let the secrets of this sacred art be passed
from parent to child to grandchild and
never forgotten.

While carrots can be grown in the Crown Tundra,
they have rather unusual growth habits.\c
When grown beneath the heaped snow,
these hardy roots tend to develop into
Iceroot Carrots.\c
When grown in tracts close to where many souls
are laid to rest, Shaderoot Carrots will be
your crop.\c
Shaderoot Carrots are a favorite treat for many
[VAR FF00(0006)]Ghost-type[VAR FF00(0000)] Pokémon, while [VAR FF00(0006)]Ice-type[VAR FF00(0000)] Pokémon
seem to delight in eating Iceroot Carrots.\c
According to old fairy tales, the steed that
the King of Bountiful Harvests rode upon
loved both of these varieties—or perhaps one
or the other.\c
Records seem to contradict one another,
with some stories speaking of a white steed
delighting in Iceroot Carrots and others
mentioning a black steed devouring
Shaderoot Carrots.

Isn’t it tough dealing with the cold here on the
tundra, with temperatures seeming to drop
lower and lower with every passing year?\c
While it’s tempting to stay indoors where it’s
cozy, don’t forget to move that body, too!\c
Try the Freezington Snow Samba today, and
get your body moving to stay warm all winter!\c
“Lift both hands in the air, wave here, wave
there, bow low, touch your toe, and freeze!
Then up we pop to start it all once more!” ♪\c
Form a circle with friends, and don’t be shy!
The Snow Samba will keep you young at heart!

Freezington Souvenir Brainstorming Sessions
(Minutes taken by the town’s tourism lead)\c
We got a lot of submissions in our last round,
so our thanks to all who contributed ideas.\c
We’ve settled on an idea for a new Freezington
souvenir sure to lure in more visitors: a shirt
featuring our own King of Bountiful Harvests!\c
By reusing the artwork from some old documents,
we should be able to keep design costs low, too.
